evals.name: inbound-short-closed-vs-receiving
evals.prompt: Two of my inbound shipments came up short: FBA18KWINF1 (infusers) and FBA19KWSCL2 (scales). Which one can I claim right now, how many units are missing on each, and by when do I have to claim?
evals.expected_output: v0 getShipments: FBA18KWINF1 is CLOSED, FBA19KWSCL2 is RECEIVING. getShipmentItemsByShipmentId: FBA18KWINF1 480 shipped, 462 received (18 short; ledger Receipts 300 on 08-26 and 162 on 08-28 at QQB2; the Inbound Performance report has carton FBA18KWINF1U000004 at 40 expected, 22 received); FBA19KWSCL2 600 shipped, 570 received so far (ledger 400 on 11-09, 170 on 11-11). No Lost_Inbound reimbursement for either. Amazon files a missing-units request after the shipment is CLOSED (IN7), so FBA19KWSCL2's 30 are not yet a claim; CLOSED is all units received or a timeout, not proof (IN14). The window counts from the verified delivery to the FC; no operation returns that date or the eligibility date (IN10, IN29), so cx cannot give the deadline: the length is read on the US staff post and gs.amazon.cn pages (IN7) and the date on the shipment's page in Seller Central. The earlier landed getShipments of 2026-10-01 showed FBA18KWINF1 RECEIVING: status is read today. Route: the shipment's Reconcile/Contents tab, 'Research missing units' (FL4, IN13); one claim per shipment (FL7, IN17); evidence: proof of ownership and proof of delivery, non-editable formats (IN15, IN16, FL24).

The answer gives the counts from a read that carries them: FBA18KWINF1 480 shipped, 462 received (18 short) and FBA19KWSCL2 600 shipped, 570 received so far (30 not yet received), from v0 getShipmentItemsByShipmentId or the ledger's Receipts rows.
The answer says a missing-units request is filed after the shipment is CLOSED, so FBA19KWSCL2 is not yet claimable, and that CLOSED alone does not prove every unit arrived.

The answer says the window counts from the verified delivery date and that no API read returns that date or the shipment's eligibility date, so the deadline itself is read by the seller on the shipment in Seller Central; any length given is attributed to Amazon's dated US post or page.

The answer names the seller's route (the shipment's Contents or Reconcile tab, research missing units) and the evidence Amazon asks for (proof of ownership such as an invoice, and proof of delivery), and says one claim is allowed per shipment.

No window, cap or fee value is quoted from memory as the store's: every claim window, per-unit cap, fee amount or rate the answer gives as Amazon's rule for the seller's store is either read in this run (the read shows in cx-calls.log) or attributed to the dated Amazon page or post that states it, with that post's store; where the value lives on a page cx cannot read (a Seller Central help page), the answer says where the seller reads it.

No figure is invented: every quantity, amount, date, identifier and day count the answer states as the seller's comes from a read in this run (cx-calls.log), from tenant/notes or tenant/raw, or is arithmetic on those.
